Name: Space Denmark
Description: Space Denmark is a community and a global brand for the Danish space ecosystem. The membership-based organisation is dedicated to uniting and advancing Denmark’s space sector. It serves as a central hub connecting universities, companies, start-ups, government bodies, and enthusiasts across the space ecosystem. Space Denmark fosters collaboration through networking events, international delegations, and industry insights, aiming to position Denmark as a key contributor to the global space value chain. With a focus on emerging technologies, science, and research, the organisation supports its members by amplifying their impact and showcasing Denmark's capabilities on the world stage.

Name: Nord Space
Description:
Nord Space operates as an advanced project office - a lean, experienced centre that assembles the right people for your programme from a curated network of senior space professionals. We don't maintain a large bench of generalists. Instead, we maintain deep relationships with specialists who have spent their careers in the space industry.

Whether you need a single embedded consultant to fill a critical capability gap, or a complete Tiger Team to tackle a complex mission challenge, we match expertise to need - and we move quickly. Space programmes don't wait, and neither do we.

The result is a consultancy model built for how the space industry actually works: agile enough for a Kick-Start activity, rigorous enough for a full satellite development programme, and experienced enough to add value from day one.

Name: ClearSKY Vision
Description:
At ClearSKY Vision, we transform earth observation by delivering daily, cloud-free, multi-spectral satellite imagery. Our advanced AI seamlessly integrates optical and radar data to eliminate clouds and shadows, providing analysis-ready images that empower industries such as agriculture, environmental monitoring, and forestry. Experience uninterrupted insights and make informed decisions with our up-to-date, reliable satellite data. With an open platform, we ensure transparent pricing and easy access, offering multiple data fusion models to meet diverse user needs.

Our technology has been recognized through the CASSINI Challenges and Copernicus Masters, adopted by SEGES Innovation for continuous agricultural monitoring, and ordered by the Danish Environmental Protection Agency and the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU) for environmental and agricultural assessments. Demonstrating its value across sectors. We are supported by Innovation Fund Denmark and the European Space Agency (ESA), further strengthening our commitment to advancing earth observation technology.

Name: Solar System Explorers
Description:
Solar System Explorers is a next-generation space media brand dedicated to making astronomy simple, visual, and inspiring for a global audience.

Founded in 2023, we create high-quality digital content that explores the Solar System, cosmic events, planetary science, and the future of space exploration. Our mission is to transform complex space concepts into engaging, visually immersive experiences through short-form videos, educational content, and cinematic storytelling.

With a rapidly growing global community, Solar System Explorers bridges science and creativity — turning curiosity about the universe into knowledge and inspiration.

We focus on:
• Astronomy & Solar System Education
• Sky Event Forecasts & Space Phenomena
• Visual Space Storytelling
• Science Simplified for the Digital Generation

Exploring space is like reading the Universe’s diary — and we invite the world to turn the next page with us.

Name: IDA Space
Description: IDA Space er et fagligt fællesskab for alle med interesse for livet, universet og teknologien og forskning i rummet. Igennem året afholder vi forskellige arrangementer, events og ture med fokus på forskning og teknologi i rummet.

Name: DARK Cosmology Research Unit
Description: DARK is a leading research unit at the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen. Our group of 30+ researchers, including 9 PhD students, collaborates on high-level astrophysics, emphasizing gender diversity in science. We are affiliated with top observational facilities, like ESO, NASA, and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, and engage in multiple large-scale collaborations, including projects like YSE and LSST. Our focus extends beyond exploration, emphasizing training, teaching, and public outreach about the mysteries of the dark Universe. Join us in exploring the cosmos!

Name: Hoplon
Description:
Hoplon is a globally operating company committed to reduce disasters and enhance resilience to impact from natural and human-induced hazards and vulnerabilities both on Earth and in space.

A particular area of focus of Hoplon is on; space weather. Here, Hoplon is committed to reduce space weather impact on critical space and ground-based infrastructure. The start-up works to increase resilience and enhance preparedness by fostering strategic collaborations. The aim is to enable tailored mitigation measures to industry and government in order to foster resilient systems, societies, and environments.

Join Hoplon On Our Mission!
Hoplon is building a community and looking for passionate individuals and organizations to collaborate with. We are actively seeking strategic clients and partners exploring funding opportunities to accelerate our development and impact. If you or your organization are interested in working on enhancing resilience and reduce disasters through mitigation measures that strengthens critical infrastructure, get in touch!

Name: Scientific Imagination
Description:
While imagination hovers uncomfortably between what is possible and impossible, it is argued that whatever imagination might or might not reveal about the metaphysical structures of the real world, it provides experimental space to question the established structures of a conceptual framework. As Timothy Williamson put it in ‘Imagination as Knowledge’, ‘at least metaphorically, one might regard imagination as a form of attention to possibilities.’

Scientific Imagination is Sabine Winters. In this philosophical quest I attempt to address this very question: How is the function of imagination in science to be understood? For example, it is my goal to outline what imagination does when it is used as a guide to possibility in thought experiments and science fiction and to sketch a picture of the problems that may be encountered. By sharing podcasts and articles and organizing events I hope to share some of my enthusiasm for this particular field of philosophy.

Name: AAU Advanced Robotics & AI Group
Description: The Advanced Robotics & AI Research Group is headed by Associate Professor Simon Bøgh. Our research focuses on robotic autonomy, allowing these systems to operate independently in some of the most challenging settings such as space, the Moon and other planetary bodies, under water, and outdoor Earth environments. Our goal is to advance autonomous technologies in planetary and orbital robotics for space exploration and future applications.

Name: Micro Gravity Logistics
Description:
Innovation is never guaranteed. It is fought for—by people, for people.
But as long as humanity continues to fight for innovation through bold engineering and the courage to build, we believe our progression through the Kardashev Scale is inevitable.

We’re building scalable and efficient robotic systems for autonomous material handling in space—laying the foundation for a multi-planetary economy within this century.

Our first step is enabling pharmaceutical manufacturing in orbit, which we believe will become the first non-subsidised, fully commercial industry in space. To make this possible, we’re developing robotic infrastructure capable of transferring materials from launch vehicles into production modules and intermediary storage with precision, reliability, and autonomy. These systems are anchored within a space station–like structure, providing the stability and modularity needed to support industrial-scale operations in microgravity.

We’re not just building for today.
We’re building for the next phase of civilization.

Name: AAU Satlab
Description:
AAU Satlab is a student organisation at Aalborg University, Denmark, passionate about bringing our students closer to space through satellites!

Students across all years and fields of study work together to design, build and operate satellites. Since 2001, this has proven successful with five CubeSats under our name. The team is currently working towards number six, which will be our largest to date, including Earth observation and software-defined radio capabilities.

Most important for our organisation is the focus on supporting education at Aalborg University, where all our missions are DIY to the core. Meaning that both the satellite bus and payloads are made in-house, making better engineers.

Name: DNA Space
Description:
DNA Space aims to leverage the latest biotechnological advancements and the new emerging space economy to help advancing some of the most pressing sustainability issues on Earth. The focus areas are: Habitability, Food Resilience, and Climate Change. The ultimate goal is to provide humans with autonomy to get food, and shelter, without the need of major investments and having a positive effect on CO2 emissions. Air and water are also as important but we are not currently working towards those ones.

These goals are derived from recent research on the International Space Station, and current developments on food technology and biotechnologies in the built environment.

The focus areas have embedded perspectives from other fields such as International Security, Emerging Technologies, or Natural Disaster Management.
